# Security and Privacy Checklist: Files and Attachments

**Purpose**: Test whether the requirements of spec 009 say enough, clearly and consistently, about who may reach a file, what is kept, what is checked and what is erased — before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-10-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [data-model.md](../data-model.md) · [contracts/files-engine.md](../contracts/files-engine.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Depth**: standard · **Audience**: the product owner, before `/speckit-implement`

## Who May Reach a File

- [ ] CHK001 Is it stated who, other than a signed-in person "of its clinic", may download a private file — the support team reading a ticket's attachments (BRD Chapter 17, OP-B-085), a patient reading their own documents — or are those actors explicitly left to later specs? [Conflict, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK002 Is "may see the record it belongs to" defined for a record that no longer exists or is hidden (a deleted patient's record, a cancelled ticket)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the answers "not found" (another clinic, another person's unattached file) and "refused" (the owner says no) specified so that a person cannot learn that a file exists in their own clinic that they may not see — or is that disclosure accepted and stated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-024, contracts §7]
- [ ] CHK004 Is it specified whether a way in may be used once or any number of times within its five minutes, and does "one audit entry per download" still hold under the chosen answer? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-022, §FR-028a]
- [ ] CHK005 Is it specified who may restore a removed file — the same people who may remove it, or others — or is that explicitly the owning page's rule, as removal is? [Completeness, Spec §FR-030a]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the conditions under which a kind may be declared public defined precisely enough to be checked ("meant for everyone", "nothing about a patient"), and is it stated that a file can never change from private to public? [Measurability, Spec §FR-027]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the builders-only kind's absence outside a developer's machine and tests written as a requirement of the spec, not only as a plan decision? [Consistency, Spec Assumptions, plan Complexity Tracking]

## Isolation Between Clinics

- [ ] CHK008 Is "the content is kept apart by clinic" stated in a way that can be objectively verified for the content itself, not only for the rows? [Measurability, Spec §FR-034]
- [ ] CHK009 Are the two readings that cross clinics (which clinics have files to scan; one public file) each bounded in the requirements by what they may return? [Completeness, data-model §6]
- [ ] CHK010 Is it specified that removing every file of one clinic (§FR-032) may be asked for only by the platform's own work, and what protects it from being pointed at the wrong clinic? [Gap, Spec §FR-032]

## What Is Checked Before a File Is Given Out

- [ ] CHK011 Does the spec say what happens to a file the scanner cannot read into — a password-protected PDF, a damaged file — as distinct from "clean", "infected" and "scanner down"? [Gap, Spec §FR-014, §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK012 Are requirements stated for content that is a valid file of an accepted type yet can act on its reader — a PDF with scripts or embedded files? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK013 Is it specified whether files already marked clean are ever scanned again when the scanner learns new signatures, or is "scanned once" an explicit decision? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK014 Is there a stated bound on how long a file may stay "being checked", and what the clinic is told when it passes — beyond the alert to the people who run the platform? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018, §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK015 Is "the type is read from its content" defined precisely enough that two implementers would accept and refuse the same files (which parts of the content are read, what counts as one of the three types)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, research R4]
- [ ] CHK016 Are limits on abuse specified or explicitly declined: how many files a person may upload and leave unattached in a day, and how fast? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions "No limit on how fast"]

## What Is Kept, Recorded and Shown

- [ ] CHK017 Is the decision to show a file's name in the notification and the audit entries reconciled with spec 008's rule that a notification holds nothing clinical, given that a name may contain a patient's name or a diagnosis? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016a, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK018 Is "operational logs" defined well enough to tell which records may hold a file's name (the audit trail, the notification) and which may not? [Clarity, Spec §FR-036]
- [ ] CHK019 Is it specified who may read the audit entries of downloads, and whether a person can see who downloaded a file they themselves cannot see? [Dependency, Spec §FR-028a, spec 007]
- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements stated for how a file's name is shown so that a name cannot act as markup or mislead about the file's type (a name ending `.pdf.exe`, right-to-left override characters)? [Gap, Spec §FR-011, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK021 Is protection of the content where it is stored (encryption at rest, who at the platform can read the store) a requirement of the spec, or only an intention of the plan for the cloud store? [Gap, research R2]
- [ ] CHK022 Does "exactly as uploaded, byte for byte" for private files conflict with any later need to show them safely (a preview, a thumbnail), and is that boundary stated? [Consistency, Spec §FR-028b, Assumptions "Showing a file"]

## Erasing and Retention

- [ ] CHK023 Does "leave nothing of it that can be read" address the platform's daily backups (SH-096), or state for how long an erased file may survive in one? [Gap, Spec §FR-033]
- [ ] CHK024 Are the three clocks — twenty-four hours unattached, thirty days removed, a class's retention period — consistent with each other in every combination the edge cases name, including a removed file that is restored after its retention period was started? [Consistency, Spec §FR-029 to §FR-031a]
- [ ] CHK025 Is it stated what an owning page must do when it never starts a retention period — is "kept for ever" then an accepted outcome, and who notices? [Completeness, Spec §FR-031]
- [ ] CHK026 Is a hold on erasing — a dispute, a legal request — addressed or explicitly excluded, given that erasing for age is automatic once a period is set? [Gap, Spec §FR-031]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the row that remains after erasing (name, size, who, when) justified against the purpose of erasing, where the name itself may be personal data? [Assumption, Spec §FR-030a]

## Acceptance and Verification

- [ ] CHK028 Can each of the security outcomes be verified as written — "every one is refused" (SC-003), "none is ever downloadable" (SC-004), "zero" (SC-005) — with the set of files and the set of ways of asking defined, not left to the tester? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003 to §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK029 Is the one refusal path that cannot be tested yet (a read-only clinic) recorded with who adds its tests and when, so it is not lost? [Traceability, Spec Assumptions, plan Constitution Check VII]
- [ ] CHK030 Are the figures the BRD does not give — five minutes, twenty-four hours, thirty days, one hour — each traceable to a stated reason and listed for the owner to confirm? [Traceability, Spec Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items most likely to need a change to the spec, in the generator's reading: CHK001 (the support team and patients are not "of the clinic"), CHK011, CHK012, CHK016, CHK023 and CHK026
